title: Choose the visual world for the ReelFlies home page
question: Your note put Streamside Stone closest. It leads here, revised for commissioned river photography; the re-roll's own direction sits beside it. Lock one, or re-roll again.

options.label: Streamside Stone, shot for real
options.lineage: Flies laid out on a riverside rock, now photographed at the water by the in-house photographer
options.thesis: The home page is a real riverside stone: flies laid out at the water's edge, and every fly on it can be picked up and added right there.
materials: white specimen cards, product photos as shot
options.viewport: A riverbank stone fills the fold, the river soft behind it: the H1, search and the two ways in sit on the shaded stone; best sellers lie on it as white specimen cards with price per fly and a working + Add; the order line is pinned below.
options.risk: Depends on a disciplined shoot: one stone, one light, one season across the banners. Until then the six slate banners stand in, and the grey must stay a working shop, never a boutique.

raised.raise: Commissioned photography carries the world: one riverbank stone for the hero, the same stone and light on every Fly Type banner, real river scenes for each Species, the Tillsonburg shop for the story.
Light marks state: at rest the stone sits in shade; the fly you point at catches raking light, and every fly you've added keeps a lit edge.
Hot-spot orange is held for one job, buying: + Add, Add to cart and the cart count, nowhere else.
Every name governs flies: point at a Fly Type or a Species and the flies it covers surface while the rest recede.
One pinned order line carries the live state: flies, patterns, total, and what's left to free shipping.
What you add is visibly placed: each added fly drops into your box on the order line.
Sizes step like a test strip: one stepped band, largest hook to smallest, previews a pattern's sizes before you commit.

options.label: The Hatch Chart
options.lineage: The printed hatch charts fly shops hand out: months across, insects down, hook sizes in the cells
options.thesis: The home page reads like a hatch chart: what's on the water this month, the sizes that match it, and the flies to add from each row.
options.viewport: A full-width chart under the header: months across with this month lit, hatch rows with their sizes; choosing a row opens its matching flies with + Add beside the chart.
options.risk: Trout-centred: bass, pike and saltwater flies don't follow hatches, so half the catalogue needs a second system, and hatch timing is regional data the owner would have to check.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: added rows take a tick, sold-out sizes a punched corner, the row you left a folded flag.
Any comparison becomes two halves: two patterns or two sizes side by side, the stronger match set heavier.
Size carries volume: this month's hatch is set loudest, the off-season rows quietest, never by colour alone.
Every step is recoverable: each chart state (month, hatch, size) has its own link you can return to.
One continuous run lights the active path: the chosen month's column glows through every row it touches.
One ink holds every state: pressing inverts, disabled dithers, so the chart never needs a second accent.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: A fly built step by step like a folded crane, every stage recoverable.
options.viewport: One square sheet with numbered steps in a margin column, folding toward a finished fly.
options.case: Fuses poorly: anglers buy tied flies, not a folding sequence, and one object at a time hides the range.
options.kept: Every step is recoverable and has its own link.

options.label: Hand-bent Neon
options.thesis: The shop's name bent in glowing glass, one continuous lit run.
options.viewport: A dark room with one lit script word and the catalogue in its glow.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dark sign shop says bar, not fly shop, and hides the photography.
options.kept: One continuous run lights the active path.
options.risk: Nightlife costume over a daytime hobby.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Patterns strung along a perforated rail like film frames, set-aside flies hanging on pins below.
options.viewport: A grain-orange field crossed by a frame rail, each frame a fly in a punched white window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: film editing means nothing to anglers, and orange over a third of the screen fights the flies.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: The shop as an early desktop: patterns in windows, dithered greys, marching ants.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows on a dithered desktop, a fly per window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no angler identification, and one-bit dither destroys the fly photography.
options.risk: Retro novelty that hides the product.

options.label: Massin Stage Page
options.thesis: The shop's voice typeset as performance, size carrying volume.
options.viewport: Colliding type across a spread, the offer shouted, the details whispered.
options.case: Fuses poorly: expressive typography crowds out the flies and the buying.
options.kept: Size carries volume, never colour alone.
options.risk: Art book, not a fly shop.

options.label: Fight Poster
options.thesis: Two flies billed head to head over a shrinking undercard.
options.viewport: Two patterns face off across a VS mark, the rest of the catalogue as undercard.
options.case: Fuses poorly: confrontation is the wrong mood for a family fly shop, and the undercard buries range.
options.risk: Loud and gimmicky; drifts toward discount.

canonCard.label: The fly-shop standard
canonCard.thesis: What fly shops ship: a river lifestyle hero with a Shop button, category tiles, best sellers, a story block and a newsletter.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed photo of an angler on a river with the headline and a Shop flies button; six category tiles below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the big fly shops by design.
